text.en: Meena watched the Prime Minister on TV. "What does the Prime Minister do?" she asked.

The Union government has three organs. The legislature is Parliament, consisting of the President, the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha. Members of the Lok Sabha are directly elected. Its normal term is five years unless it is dissolved sooner. The Rajya Sabha continues as a body while members retire by rotation.
The President is the head of state and acts on the advice of the Council of Ministers. The Prime Minister leads the Council of Ministers, which is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha.
The Supreme Court is the highest court and protects the Constitution. The judiciary is independent and can review laws. Parliament makes laws, passes the budget and watches the executive.
The Union government has three organs.

board.text: Parliament

text.en: The legislature is Parliament, consisting of the President, the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha.

board.text: Lok Sabha

text.en: Members of the Lok Sabha are directly elected. Its normal term is five years from its first meeting, unless it is dissolved sooner. The Rajya Sabha continues as a body, with members retiring by rotation.

board.text: Rajya Sabha

text.en: The President is the constitutional head of state and acts according to the advice of the Council of Ministers. The President may ask the Council to reconsider its advice once.

board.text: President

text.en: The Prime Minister leads the Council of Ministers. The Council is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha.

board.text: Prime Minister

text.en: The Supreme Court is the highest court and protects the Constitution.

board.text: Supreme Court

text.en: The judiciary is independent and can review laws.

board.text: Parliament

text.en: Parliament makes laws, passes the budget and watches the executive.

board.text: Lok Sabha

text.en: The legislature makes laws. The executive carries out laws and runs public administration. The judiciary interprets laws and decides disputes.

board.text: The three organs have different responsibilities

text.en: The two Houses are the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha. The President is part of Parliament under the Constitution and does not sit in either House as an elected member.

board.text: Parliament includes the President and two Houses

text.en: Voters elect members to represent parliamentary constituencies. Its normal five-year term can end earlier if it is dissolved.

board.text: The Lok Sabha represents the people directly

text.en: It is not dissolved as a whole. The Constitution provides for roughly one third of its members to retire every second year.

board.text: The Rajya Sabha is a continuing chamber

text.en: Elected members of state legislative assemblies elect their states’ representatives. The President also nominates members with special knowledge or experience in specified fields.

board.text: States take part in choosing Rajya Sabha members

text.en: The Speaker presides over the Lok Sabha. The Vice-President is the Chairperson of the Rajya Sabha by virtue of that office.

board.text: Presiding officers conduct the work of the Houses

text.en: A Bill is a proposed law. After introduction it may be examined, discussed and amended before members vote.

board.text: An ordinary Bill usually can begin in either House

text.en: An ordinary Bill normally needs agreement on the same text. It is then presented to the President for assent.

board.text: Both Houses generally agree on the ordinary Bill’s text

text.en: A committee can study details and report to Parliament. Members can use that analysis when debating a proposed law.

board.text: Committees examine proposals more closely

text.en: A Money Bill can originate only in the Lok Sabha. The Rajya Sabha can make recommendations within fourteen days, and the Lok Sabha can accept or reject them.

board.text: Money Bills follow a special procedure

text.en: The Constitution provides for an annual financial statement. Parliament scrutinises public money, and the Lok Sabha votes on demands for grants.

board.text: The budget describes estimated receipts and spending

text.en: Members use tools such as questions and committee scrutiny. The executive must be able to explain its decisions to Parliament.

board.text: Parliament can ask the executive to explain itself

text.en: The electoral college includes elected members of both Houses of Parliament and elected members of the relevant legislative assemblies. It is not a direct public election.

board.text: The President is elected indirectly

text.en: The President appoints the Prime Minister. The other ministers are appointed on the Prime Minister’s advice.

board.text: The President appoints the Prime Minister

text.en: The Council is headed by the Prime Minister. If the President asks it to reconsider advice, the President acts according to the advice after reconsideration.

board.text: The Council of Ministers advises the President

text.en: The Council of Ministers remains accountable to the Lok Sabha as a team. A government that loses the House’s confidence cannot normally continue as before.

board.text: Collective responsibility connects the executive to the House

text.en: When both Houses are not in session together and immediate action is needed, the President can issue an ordinance under Article One Hundred and Twenty-Three. It must be laid before both Houses and is temporary.

board.text: An ordinance is temporary legislation

text.en: The Attorney General gives legal advice to the Government of India and performs legal duties assigned under the Constitution.

board.text: The Attorney General is the Union’s constitutional law officer

text.en: The Supreme Court can decide certain disputes directly and hear appeals. It also has constitutional roles such as enforcing Fundamental Rights.

board.text: The Supreme Court heads the Indian judiciary

text.en: Courts may examine whether a law or government act complies with the Constitution. This helps keep public authority within constitutional limits.

board.text: Judicial review checks constitutional limits

text.en: Courts need to decide cases according to law without improper pressure. Constitutional arrangements help protect that independence.

board.text: Judicial independence supports fair decisions

text.en: Passing a law points to Parliament, administering a policy points to the executive, and deciding a legal dispute points to the judiciary.

problem.en: Who is the head of government in India?

text.en: The Prime Minister.
Leader of the Council of Ministers.
Responsible to the Lok Sabha.

problem.en: An ordinary Bill begins in the Rajya Sabha. What usually happens before it can become an Act?

text.en: The Houses consider and pass the same text.

why.en: Either House can generally introduce an ordinary Bill.

text.en: The Bill goes to the President for assent.

why.en: The board shows the usual route in which both Houses agree.

problem.en: The Lok Sabha passes a Money Bill and the Rajya Sabha offers changes. Must the Lok Sabha accept them?

text.en: The Rajya Sabha can make recommendations within fourteen days.

why.en: A Money Bill has a special procedure.

text.en: The Lok Sabha may accept or reject those recommendations.

why.en: This differs from the ordinary Bill route.

problem.en: A court examines whether an Act violates a Fundamental Right. What function is it exercising?

text.en: The court compares the Act with the Constitution.
Examining compliance with the Constitution is judicial review.

why.en: It is one check on public power.

prompt.en: A friend says The Rajya Sabha is dissolved every five years. How will you reply?

requiredIdeas.en: The Lok Sabha is elected for five years.
